doc.title: Anat Cohen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2021

title: Mango Blue Afro-Cuban band and learning to dance on stage
summary: Playing in a Boston Afro-Cuban band beside Miguel Zenon taught her to dance and be relaxed on stage.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Did the hang translate, help translate into your stage presence, which I observe as welcoming and an addition to what you can present?

You know it’s interesting, I mean first of all I’m glad you feel it’s welcoming and you know I don’t know if it’s the hang — I think part of what made me feel comfortable on stage was being part of an Afro-Cuban band — it’s a band in Boston called, it used to be called Mango Blue, then it became Mango Blues, and I was in the saxophone section with Miguel Zenon, the great alto player. And I didn’t know much about Afro-Cuban music or all the South American rhythm, it was all new to me, but another thing that was definitely new to me is dancing. And being on stage, playing, you know, sometimes there would be a long piano solo and everybody, basically looking at the audience everybody is dancing, and I’m realizing okay I cannot just be on stage standing still. It’s not part of the culture, it’s not part of the music, so I was very embarrassed at the beginning and then I’m like okay I can just move and then slowly I got more relaxed into it, and then when there’d be long solos I would just leave my saxophone on stage and go in the audience and just start dancing with people and dance with Miguel on the stage looking, learning the steps. And I think after being able to not worry about what other people think because I’m dancing, it’s just a whole other cultural aspect that is not — I didn’t learn in Israel. I think after that, being on stage and just playing and concentrating on the music and
moving to the moment and being in the moment I don’t think about the stage as a stage. I just think it’s like let’s just all celebrate the moment.
